# Senzor

> Senzor is an open-source, privacy-first observability platform for modern engineering teams. It unifies infrastructure monitoring, application performance monitoring, distributed tracing, log management, error tracking, uptime monitoring, web analytics, real user monitoring, and AI-powered operational intelligence into a single platform. All data is hosted in the EU with full GDPR compliance.

## Services

- [Infrastructure Monitoring](https://senzor.dev/features/server): Real-time server, container, and VM monitoring for CPU, memory, disk I/O, and network throughput. Uses a lightweight bash agent deployed as a systemd service or Docker container. Supports Linux (Ubuntu, Debian, CentOS, RHEL, Alpine). Includes Nginx and Traefik integration.
- [Database Observability](https://senzor.dev/features/database): Query latency profiling, active connection monitoring, and operations-per-second tracking. Supports MongoDB and Redis.
- [Firebase Monitoring](https://senzor.dev/features/firebase): Agentless Firebase Authentication monitoring. Tracks user growth, daily and monthly active users, MFA enrollment rates, email verification rates, and auth provider distribution using encrypted credential polling.
- [Web Analytics](https://senzor.dev/features/web-analytics): Cookie-less, GDPR-compliant traffic analytics. Tracks page views, unique visitors, referrers, geographic distribution, and device breakdowns without storing personal data.
- [Real User Monitoring](https://senzor.dev/features/rum): Browser-side performance monitoring capturing Core Web Vitals (LCP, FID, CLS), network call latency, frontend JavaScript exceptions, and rage click detection. Deployed via a lightweight JavaScript SDK.
- [Application Performance Monitoring](https://senzor.dev/features/apm): Distributed tracing across microservices with automatic framework instrumentation, end-to-end trace waterfall visualizations, and database and external API call profiling. Supports OpenTelemetry OTLP ingestion.
- [Background Task Monitoring](https://senzor.dev/features/tasks): Monitors queues, cron jobs, and background workers. Tracks execution times, failure rates, retry behaviors, queue depth, and dead-letter queue detection. Supports OpenTelemetry OTLP ingestion.
- [Global Error Tracking](https://senzor.dev/features/errors): Automatic exception capture with intelligent fingerprinting, full stack trace rendering, cross-service impact analysis, and resolution state tracking.
- [Centralized Log Management](https://senzor.dev/features/logs): High-throughput log ingestion via HTTP API. Advanced MQL (Monitoring Query Language) filtering engine with automatic trace correlation and live-tail streaming.
- [Uptime Monitoring](https://senzor.dev/features/uptime): High-frequency synthetic HTTP checks verifying external endpoint availability. Tracks global response times and records downtime incidents.
- [Alerts and Incident Routing](https://senzor.dev/features/alerts): Multi-condition threshold-based alert policies across all telemetry streams. Routes incidents via Webhooks, Slack, and Email. Supports MQL-based custom alert triggers and incident lifecycle management.
- [MCP Server](https://senzor.dev/features/mcp): Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enabling AI agents to query, summarize, and analyze telemetry data using natural language. Supports SSE transport. Compatible with Claude Code, Cursor, and other MCP-capable clients.
- [Native OpenTelemetry Support](https://senzor.dev/features/opentelemetry): Vendor-neutral OTLP HTTP-compatible endpoints for traces and metrics. Supports Go, Java, Python, and Rust applications. Automatic translation of OTLP payloads into Senzor dashboard schemas with standard Semantic Conventions support.
- [Saved Views](https://senzor.dev/features/views): Custom dashboards aggregating metrics, logs, and traces across the entire stack. Drag-and-drop widget canvas with cross-service data aggregation and strict tenant data isolation.

## Technical Architecture

- **Deployment**: Available as a managed cloud service (EU-hosted) or self-hosted via Docker Compose and Kubernetes.
- **API Base URL**: `https://api.senzor.dev/api`
- **Data Ingestion**: Outbound-only telemetry over HTTPS (port 443). SDKs use in-memory ring buffers with exponential backoff retry to prevent data loss during connectivity issues.
- **Correlation**: Logs, metrics, and traces are automatically correlated. An APM trace failure links directly to associated server logs and RUM sessions.
- **Query Language**: MQL (Monitoring Query Language) for filtering and querying across all telemetry types.
- **Data Tier**: Pooled globally across workspaces rather than per-service limits.

## Integrations

- **OpenTelemetry**: Native OTLP HTTP endpoints for traces and metrics ingestion from any OpenTelemetry-compatible application or collector.
- **MCP (Model Context Protocol)**: SSE-based MCP server for AI agent integration. Configurable via Claude Code CLI, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible client.
- **Notification Channels**: Slack, Email, and Webhooks for alert routing.
- **Server Agent**: Supports Nginx status monitoring and Traefik API integration.
- **Log Ingestion**: HTTP API accepting JSON payloads with structured log levels, messages, and custom attributes.

## Security and Compliance

- **GDPR**: Senzor acts as a Data Processor under GDPR. All infrastructure is hosted in the European Union.
- **Encryption**: AES-256 encryption at rest. TLS 1.3 encryption in transit.
- **Authentication**: Firebase Authentication with email OTP on login and optional TOTP-based multi-factor authentication.
- **Access Control**: Role-based access control (RBAC) with tenant data isolation. Granular API key permissions for MCP and log ingestion.
- **Data Retention**: Tied to billing plan. Starter: 3 days, Pro: 15 days, Business: 30 days. Data is cryptographically expunged after TTL expiry.
- **PII Policy**: Users are prohibited from transmitting clear-text PII or PHI within custom log messages or traces.

## Plans

Senzor offers five tiers: Free, Starter, Pro, Business, and Enterprise. All plans include access to every service. Plans differ in data retention (3 to 30 days), ingestion volume, and support level. See the pricing page for current details.

## What We Do Not Do

Senzor does not provide CDN services, DNS hosting, cloud compute, CI/CD pipelines, code deployment, APM for frontend-only applications without a backend, or synthetic browser testing. Senzor does not sell, share, or monetize user telemetry data.

- [Infrastructure Monitoring Setup](https://senzor.dev/docs/server): Server agent installation via bash script, Docker Compose, or non-interactive CI mode.

- [Web Analytics Setup](https://senzor.dev/docs/web-analytics): JavaScript tracking snippet installation and domain allowlisting.
- [Real User Monitoring Setup](https://senzor.dev/docs/rum): Browser SDK installation for React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, Angular, Astro, and plain HTML.
- [APM Setup](https://senzor.dev/docs/apm): OpenTelemetry SDK configuration for Node.js, Python, Go, Java, and Rust.
- [Background Task Monitoring Setup](https://senzor.dev/docs/tasks): OpenTelemetry-based task and queue worker instrumentation.
- [Error Tracking Setup](https://senzor.dev/docs/errors): Exception capture configuration across backend services.
- [Log Management Setup](https://senzor.dev/docs/logs): HTTP log ingestion API reference and structured logging guide.
- [Uptime Monitoring Setup](https://senzor.dev/docs/uptime): Endpoint registration and check frequency configuration.
- [MCP Server Setup](https://senzor.dev/docs/mcp): MCP SSE endpoint configuration for Claude Code, Cursor, and other AI clients.
- [Alerts Setup](https://senzor.dev/docs/alerts): Alert policy creation, condition configuration, and notification channel routing.
- [OpenTelemetry Setup](https://senzor.dev/docs/opentelemetry): OTLP collector configuration and SDK integration guide.
- [FAQ](https://senzor.dev/docs/faq): Frequently asked questions about security, compliance, architecture, and billing.
- [Self-Hosting Guide](https://github.com/Senzops/.github/blob/dev/SELF_HOSTING.md): Docker Compose and Kubernetes deployment manifests for on-premise installation.
